title: Model Weight Licensing and Usage Safeguards - Template (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope
This template is intended for use when Redwood or a customer needs to govern the licensing and permitted uses of model weights ("weights") and derivative model artifacts provided to a counterparty ("Licensee"). The goal is to balance operational flexibility with safeguards for data protection, IP, export controls, and commercial risk.

Status
- Draft for internal review by Legal, Security, and Applied ML
- Do not send to third parties in current form; placeholders remain.

High-level summary (short)
- Grant: narrow, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use specified weights for permitted uses (evaluation, inference in production) with explicit prohibitions on redistribution, resale, and unauthorized fine-tuning unless separately agreed.
- Data protections: obligations around PII, logging, retention, and KMS/HSM controls for any derivative training data.
- Security & audits: indemnities, audit rights, and breach notification timelines.
- Termination & return: obligations to delete or return weights and derivatives on termination.

Key contract clauses (recommended language - placeholders in brackets)
1) Definitions
- "Weights": the binary model parameters, configuration files, and associated metadata delivered under this Agreement.
- "Derivative Model": any model resulting from fine-tuning, adaptation, or transformation of the Weights.
- "Permitted Uses": [evaluation, internal inference for Customer product X, supply chain verification] - specify explicitly.

2) License Grant
- Subject to Licensee's compliance with this Agreement, Redwood (or Licensor) grants Licensee a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to use the Weights solely for the Permitted Uses during the Term. Any use outside Permitted Uses requires prior written consent and may trigger commercial terms.

3) Prohibited Activities
- Licensee shall not: (a) redistribute, resell, sublicense, or make available the Weights to third parties; (b) use Weights for biometric identification, targeted surveillance, or law enforcement profiling without explicit approval; (c) attempt to reverse engineer or extract training data or recreate the training dataset; (d) export or re-export in violation of applicable export controls; (e) deploy Derivative Models in regulated contexts (healthcare, finance) unless compliance controls and insurance are in place.

4) Fine-tuning and Derivatives
- Fine-tuning is permitted only if explicitly allowed in Schedule A. If permitted, Derivative Models remain subject to the same restrictions as the Weights unless otherwise agreed. Licensee must maintain provenance metadata and provide Redwood, upon request, a redacted description of fine-tuning datasets and objectives for safety review (confidential).

5) Data Protection and Handling of Personal Data
- Licensee shall not input any Personal Data into any processes that will be used to fine-tune the Weights without prior written approval and a data processing addendum.
- If inference logs or telemetry that include Personal Data are stored by Licensee, Licensee must implement access controls, encryption at rest and in transit, and a retention schedule not to exceed [90] days unless otherwise agreed.

6) Security Controls
- Licensee shall implement industry standard security practices: encryption (AES-256 or equivalent), KMS/HSM for key management, RBAC for access to weights and artifacts, and logging of access events.
- For on-prem deployments, Licensee shall provide a snapshot of security posture (self-attestation) and allow a scoped security review by Redwood (remote) upon reasonable notice.

7) Audit Rights and Evidence
- Redwood may, no more than once per 12 months and upon reasonable notice, audit Licensee's compliance with use restrictions and security controls. Audits shall be scoped, use minimally invasive methods, and protect Licensee's confidential business information. Licensee shall provide redacted logs and attestations for the audit.

8) Incident Notification
- Licensee must notify Redwood within 48 hours of discovering any suspected compromise, misuse, or accidental exposure of Weights or Derivative Models. Notification must include a description of the incident, affected artifacts, initial containment steps, and planned remediation timeline.

9) Indemnity and Liability
- Licensee indemnifies Licensor for claims arising from Licensee's unauthorized use of the Weights. Liability caps to be negotiated; recommend mirroring existing SaaS liability ceilings but consider higher caps for redistribution breaches.

10) Export, Sanctions, and Compliance
- Licensee represents it will not export, re-export, or otherwise make available the Weights to any country, person, or entity restricted by applicable export control laws or sanctions. Licensee must notify Licensor if it becomes subject to sanctions or export restrictions.

11) Confidentiality
- The Weights and related model metadata are Confidential Information. The Agreement should reference the main NDA/confidentiality section and set specific handling rules for model artifacts.

12) Termination and Post-Term Obligations
- Upon termination or expiration, Licensee shall: (a) cease use of the Weights for new inference; (b) certify deletion of all copies of the Weights and Derivative Models (and provide evidence where practical); (c) if return is required, transfer securely via SFTP or encrypted container to a designated address.

13) Remedies
- In the event of material breach (including unauthorized redistribution or reverse engineering), Redwood may seek injunctive relief and damages. Include right to suspend license pending cure period.

14) Insurance and Compliance Attestations
- For Licenses that allow fine-tuning or hosting customer data, Licensee must maintain cyber insurance (recommended minimum $5M) and provide periodic SOC2-Type II reports or equivalent.

Operational annexes (examples to attach as Schedules)
- Schedule A: Permitted Uses and Prohibited Use Table (tick boxes for evaluation, prod inference, fine-tuning, redistribution)
- Schedule B: Security Requirements (minimum crypto, key management, network segmentation for on-prem)
- Schedule C: Data Handling & Retention Template (fields to populate by customer and retained as contract exhibit)
- Schedule D: Audit & Evidence Request Form

Practical negotiation notes (internal guidance)
- Evaluate customer risk profile: Are they a regulated entity? Will they host PII? Will they seek to fine-tune? Answers determine whether to allow fine-tuning and the evidence required.
- Avoid blanket "no-fine-tuning" positions for SMB customers where allowed uses are narrow; use commercial terms instead (e.g., per-model fee, monitoring obligations).
- For on-prem deployments, increase frequency of attestations and require a minimum security baseline; consider mandatory quarterly compliance checks for high-risk customers.

Unresolved questions / decision points
- What is Redwood's default stance on derivative model ownership when the customer pays for fine-tuning compute? (retain joint IP vs customer owns derivative)
- Standard retention period for inference logs: 30, 90, or 180 days? (security vs product debugging tradeoffs)
- Default insurance minimum and scope for small customers vs enterprise.

Checklist before sending to counterparties
- [ ] Populate Schedule A with concrete Permitted Uses
- [ ] Confirm whether fine-tuning is permitted and, if so, attach Schedule C
- [ ] Fill in export control and sanctions clause specifics per counterparty domicile
- [ ] Obtain SOC2 or equivalent for hosting customers or require attestation for on-prem
- [ ] Coordinate with Applied ML on acceptable provenance metadata disclosures
- [ ] Legal to review indemnity and liability cap language

Example negotiation redlines (short guidance)
- If customer requests redistribution rights: counter with time-limited, scoped sublicensing instead of open redistribution and additional fees.
- If customer requests unlimited reverse engineering carve-out: reject; propose a narrow carve-out for interoperability only after additional security and contractual safeguards.

Appendix: Sample permissive clause for open-research collaborations
- For research partnerships where model weights are intended to be openly shared, use a separate Open-Research License that: (a) includes attribution, (b) disclaims warranties, (c) prohibits commercial resale without separate agreement, and (d) includes a simple citation requirement.

Notes to reviewers
- Cross-check with existing DPA templates and the Private Deployments Annex for overlapping privacy/security obligations.
- Coordinate with Sales on pricing impacts of granting fine-tuning or redistribution rights (usually increases commercial value).

References / internal links
- PM brief: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PL/overview
- Security playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/84012345/Security+Playbook

Change log
- 2024-09-04 (AP): Initial draft skeleton and clauses
- 2024-10-12 (MR): Added audit and incident notification language
- 2025-01-10 (LT): Security annex placeholders expanded

Author notes / quick TODOs
- Leah to draft Schedule B minimum crypto standards (deadline: 2025-01-17)
- Applied ML to confirm recommended provenance fields (ticket: SEC-2345)
- Legal to propose default retention value and insurance floor

Drafting cues (tone and approach)
- Keep license narrow and specific; prefer enumerated permitted uses rather than broad categories.
- Use examples sparingly to avoid unintended scope expansion.
- Keep operational controls in Schedules to allow clause reuse without legal rework.

End of document
